box64.note: The pinned Box64 Vulkan wrapper structurally represents vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR, but a direct libandroid/AHardwareBuffer bridge for arbitrary x86_64 guest code is not verified. No runtime claim is made.

androidTransport.candidate: AHardwareBuffer or external-memory FD chosen from measured device capabilities
androidTransport.note: Host-side AHardwareBuffer capability and transport evidence never proves the guest/Wine import or visible WSI path. AHardwareBuffer is memory/image state, not VkSurfaceKHR.

guestGraphicsTransport.note: SCM_RIGHTS plus resource/generation/sequence binding and a guest receive helper are implemented as isolated primitives. The authenticated runtime session, Vulkan import into the Wine/DXVK device and GPU synchronization remain separate gates.

capabilityDiscovery.note: Capability discovery is diagnostic evidence only. Extensions or import-query success do not prove guest import, swapchain or a host-visible Present.

surfaceBackend.note: Wine win32u stores the VkSurfaceKHR returned by p_vulkan_surface_create as the host surface handle. The opt-in headless diagnostic can create such a surface without visibility; production still requires a host-visible presentation backend.

rejectedRoutes.route: send ANativeWindow pointer over Display Bridge socket
rejectedRoutes.reason: ANativeWindow is process-local opaque state; a pointer value is not a transferable cross-process handle.
AHardwareBuffer is a transferable image/memory primitive. Wine requires p_vulkan_surface_create to return a host VkSurfaceKHR used by later surface and swapchain calls.

rejectedRoutes.route: treat GDI window_surface.flush as DXVK Present
rejectedRoutes.reason: Wine Vulkan uses the graphics driver's pVulkanInit/WSI contract; GDI framebuffer flush does not establish a Vulkan surface or swapchain.

rejectedRoutes.route: reuse wineandroid.drv as the DXVK WSI backend
rejectedRoutes.reason: Pinned Wine 11 wineandroid.drv exposes pOpenGLInit but no pVulkanInit.

rejectedRoutes.route: promote Android-to-Android AHardwareBuffer transport to guest graphics readiness
rejectedRoutes.reason: Distinct Android processes prove host handle transfer only. Box64/Wine receive, Vulkan import and synchronization remain separate guest gates.

rejectedRoutes.route: enable production VK_KHR_win32_surface from the headless diagnostic
rejectedRoutes.reason: The diagnostic surface is explicitly invisible and opt-in. It may prove Vulkan surface/swapchain mechanics but cannot satisfy Android-visible Present.

rejectedRoutes.route: treat external-memory extension mapping as imported PocketPC graphics resource evidence
rejectedRoutes.reason: Wine external Win32-to-fd mapping exposes a mechanism; it does not prove a broker FD was received, bound to the correct resource, imported into the active VkDevice or synchronized.

targetArchitecture.phase1: Android host proves AHardwareBuffer allocation plus same-process AF_UNIX handle round-trip.
targetArchitecture.phase2: A dedicated Android :gpu_probe process receives the transferable AHardwareBuffer handle, validates descriptor and bytes, and returns evidence from a distinct PID.
targetArchitecture.phase3: Probe physical-device WSI and external-resource capabilities and run the canonical AHardwareBuffer import-property query without promoting readiness.
targetArchitecture.phase4: Expose the exact Wine Vulkan v47 ABI, external Win32-handle to fd mappings, and an opt-in headless diagnostic surface while production surface creation stays fail-closed.
targetArchitecture.phase5: Use SCM_RIGHTS plus descriptor/ownership binding to receive one exact graphics resource on the guest side; connect that primitive to the authenticated runtime broker.
targetArchitecture.phase6: Import the received external resource into the same host VkDevice used by Wine/DXVK and prove memory compatibility.
targetArchitecture.phase7: Implement external semaphore/fence ownership and prove guest/host synchronization for the imported resource.
targetArchitecture.phase8: Use headless diagnostic WSI for non-visible DXVK surface/swapchain/Present evidence without promoting production readiness.
targetArchitecture.phase9: Select and implement one host-visible VkSurfaceKHR/presentation architecture for Android.
targetArchitecture.phase10: Implement visible surface creation, presentation support, acquire/render/present ownership and swapchain presentation.
targetArchitecture.phase11: Run D3D11 Present smoke and require a host-visible frame before recording production graphics evidence.
targetArchitecture.phase12: Only then unblock controlled Roblox/DXVK application attempts and record gameplay evidence separately.
